proposed.text: A formwork project requires 50 pieces of 1×6×8 lumber. How many total board feet are needed (no waste)?

options.text: 160 BF — result of an incorrect per-piece multiplier of 3.2
200 BF — the correct total (4 BF/piece × 50 pieces) for 1×6×8 lumber
240 BF — result of omitting the ÷12 step in the board-foot formula
400 BF — result of using board length as the direct multiplier

proposed.rationale: BF per piece: (1 × 6 × 8) ÷ 12 = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 BF per board. Total: 50 boards × 4 BF/board = 200 BF. [A]: 160 BF results from 50 × 3.2 (incorrect per-piece calculation). [C]: 240 BF results from 50 × 4.8 or (1 × 6 × 8) without division. [D]: 400 BF results from 50 × 8 (using length as multiplier).
proposed.explanation: 160 BF results from 50 × 3.2 (incorrect per-piece calculation). 240 BF results from 50 × 4.8 or (1 × 6 × 8) without division. 400 BF results from 50 × 8 (using length as multiplier). BF per piece: (1 × 6 × 8) ÷ 12 = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 BF per board. Total: 50 boards × 4 BF/board = 200 BF. Calculate board feet per piece first, then multiply by quantity.
